doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Baby Grand and no steady income
summary: He worked Newark, Long Island and the Baby Grands but earned no steady living, and family never came.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: It helped to renew your spirit. Then another part of your career begins, where you’re playing little clubs, like the Baby Grand, like you were saying, in Long Island and all over, but you’re still struggling, but you’re able to make a humble living as a jazz singer. Is that accurate?
No. It wasn’t enough. I wasn’t able to make a steady living . . .
Ah. That’s the distinction that has to be made.

. . . that would support me until things got in shape or I could find someone who could handle things for me. I had a sister who lived there, but they never – none of my folks ever wanted to be around me. I have never had any of them at a performance of mine. No-one in the family. What are you going to do? So I couldn’t talk to them about the business end, because they had to come around.
